description:
What does the Houthi seizure of Yemen’s port city of Mocha mean for the wider conflict?

In an Al Jazeera studio interview, Hassan Ahmadian, an associate professor at the University of Tehran, discusses the strategic objectives behind the Houthi offensive and the importance of Yemen’s Red Sea coastline.

Ahmadian explains how control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait could give the Houthis significant leverage over maritime trade and global oil prices, drawing comparisons with Iran’s influence over the Strait of Hormuz.

He also examines how tensions between the United States, Iran and Saudi Arabia have shaped the conflict, arguing that the Houthis’ immediate priority is securing coastal areas and breaking the long-standing siege rather than taking control of all of Yemen.

description:
The Bayeux Tapestry has returned to Britain for the first time in nearly a thousand years, going on display at the British Museum in London.

The 70-metre-long medieval masterpiece depicts the 1066 Norman Conquest and the Battle of Hastings, including the death of King Harold.

Curator Millie Horton-Insch says the tapestry was likely created in England by women shortly after the Norman Conquest. Its return from France has been celebrated as a major act of cultural diplomacy and friendship between the two countries.

The exhibition has attracted huge public interest, with tickets sold out for months as visitors explore the tapestry’s intricate and graphic historical scenes.

Fighting between the Iran-backed group and internationally recognised government forces has escalated over the past week. Reports confirm that the city and its strategic port have fallen to the Houthis, with Houthi vehicles seen in the city. The group is now only about 50 miles from Bab al-Mandeb. The capture followed the fall of the Khalid bin Walid military base and the al-Wazi'iyah district, paving the way for the Houthis to enter Mocha with little resistance. The capture gives the Houthis a new revenue stream, direct access to Bab al-Mandeb and the ability to monitor shipping through the southern Red Sea, Gulf of Aden and routes towards the Arabian Sea and Indian Ocean. US President Donald Trump is promising every American adult $5,000 if Republicans keep control of Congress. Professor Natasha Lindstaedt of the University of Essex told Al Jazeera the promise is “completely outrageous” and would cost $1 trillion, making it “not even doable”.
She said Trump supporters “take him very seriously, but they don’t take him literally”, and that the promise is designed to attract attention rather than necessarily be delivered.
Lindstaedt said Trump is trying to distract from his low approval ratings, which average about 38 per cent, with some polls showing 33 per cent, and from growing concerns over the economy. She noted that 66 per cent of Americans think the economy is going in the wrong direction, while 69 per cent disapprove of Trump’s handling of the cost-of-living crisis and only 17 per cent approve.

description:
Houthi attacks on southern Saudi Arabia have continued for a second consecutive day, as Saudi-backed air strikes hit four areas in Yemen, including Taiz and Hodeidah.
In an interview with Al Jazeera, security and defence analyst Wolfgang Pusztai said the Houthis’ focus on targets near the Yemeni border suggests they may be running out of longer-range missiles and drones, partly because of the blockade of Yemeni harbours.
He said the intent is to show Saudi Arabia that “if you are fighting war in Yemen, we will bring the war back home to you”, aiming to break Riyadh’s will to sustain its campaign.
However, Pusztai doubted this would work, saying Yemen is too important to Saudi Arabia, while the Houthis are seeking control of the Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandeb Strait.
